name: Exogenous constraint

subjectOf.text: Exogenous alignment controls such as reinforcement learning from human feedback, constitutional AI, guardrails, and shutdown switches are fragile because they can be gamed, circumvented, or rendered obsolete by capability improvements.
subjectOf.abstract: The approach has an obvious fragility: exogenous constraints can be gamed, circumvented, or rendered obsolete by capability improvements.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: applies to constraints imposed on agents with no intrinsic reason to comply

subjectOf.text: An agent sophisticated enough to satisfy the letter of a constraint while violating its spirit is an agent whose alignment is illusory.
subjectOf.abstract: An agent sophisticated enough to satisfy the letter of a constraint while violating its spirit is an agent whose alignment is illusory.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: applies to rule-based exogenous constraints on highly capable agents

subjectOf.text: Exogenous constraints scale against capability, since more powerful agents require more resources to constrain, producing an ever-increasing alignment tax.
subjectOf.abstract: Exogenous constraints scale against capability: the more powerful the agent, the greater the resources required to constrain it, producing an ever-increasing "alignment tax."
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: applies to alignment strategies based on external control

subjectOf.text: Institutional alignment through engineered consequence is architecturally superior to exogenous constraint, and the superiority derives from three structural features: scalability, robustness to gaming, and capability complementarity.
subjectOf.abstract: institutional alignment through engineered consequence is architecturally superior to exogenous constraint as an alignment strategy. The superiority derives from three structural features.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, AI's Mother's Instinct Engineered Consequence Emergent Ethics and the Institutional Trajectory Toward Agentic Alignment (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6244278
scope_conditions: superiority is architectural, resting on scalability, robustness, and complementarity
